text:
'Passive movements' are movements of a body part produced by an external force—such as a therapist, machine, or gravity—rather than by the person's own muscle contraction. They are used in physical therapy and clinical assessment to maintain range of motion, prevent stiffness, and evaluate joint mobility or tone. The claim that they were first described in ancient Greek gymnastics mainly to train athletes is not supported by the standard clinical definition.
